thread:
Deploy Bot: Canary rollout v2.8 started to canary pool 'cpu-canaries' at 08:03 UTC
Maya: seeing a spike in 5xxs from canary group, starting ~08:05
Alex: getting pages from PD about SLO burn - who is oncall? @Maya are you looking?
Maya: I'm on it, checking logs. No obvious code exceptions, looks like latency/timeouts that turn into 5xx from the proxy
Sindre: paging: PD alert: SLO_Latency_5m > 10% for model-serving-prod (incident id pd_90234)
PagerDuty Bot: <@Sindre> acknowledged incident pd_90234
Jess: our canary dashboard is missing key panels, pinging metrics team; think Grafana got a variable rename in last change
Maya: ugh, can't easily see per-route error rates because the label name changed from 'route' to 'endpoint' in prometheus scrape
Alex: noisy alerts are drowning the signal. Could we mute the canary alerts briefly? don't want to lose real infra alerts
Chris: I can mute the noisy rule for model-serving-prod in alertmanager for 15m: /am mute rule_id=rule_83 duration=15m
Maya: doing quick local traces, payloads look normal. One suspicion: new routing fallback to older quantized model causing timeouts under concurrent KV cache pressure
Sindre: is there a kill-switch for rollout? feature flag 'rollout_v2' exists
Alex: yes: `/flags rollback_v2 --off` or via feature-flag service: `curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/set -d 'flag=rollout_v2&state=false'`
Maya: I'm going to flip it now
Maya: `curl -s -X POST https://flags.internal/api/set -d 'flag=rollout_v2&state=false'` -> 200 OK
Deploy Bot: Canary rollout v2.8 paused by Maya
PagerDuty Bot: <@Maya> resolved incident pd_90234
Jess: we still have noisy historical alerts; we should reopen a follow-up to fix dashboard and alert rule noise
Chris: will roll back the canary group to previous stable model on host pool c-canary-3: `/deploy rollback --group canary --to stable-20250214`
Alex: rolling back now, stop sending canary traffic to v2.8
Alex: rollback started... logs show old model restored on c-canary-3
Sindre: monitoring latency and error rates... looks like 5xx back to baseline ~08:18
Maya: customers with long-lived sessions might have seen errors between 08:05-08:17; DevEx flagged a few support tickets
Jess: action items: 1) fix prometheus label rename (metrics) 2) update canary dashboard panels 3) make a dedicated canary alerting mute step in rollout runbook 4) add an explicit kill-switch play in release docs
Chris: I'll open the follow-up and assign: #jira INF-4873
Maya: big one: SLO burn confusion -- our oncall playbook didn't list which SLO to burn for rollouts. We need a single canonical SLO for release fatigue
Alex: agreed. also we need a temp dashboard that surfaces canary-specific error budget consumption
Sindre: thanks all. If anything else pops, ping oncall. We'll draft an incident summary after lunch.
Deploy Bot: Note: automatic canary promotion halted
Jess: filing post-incident notes in #postmortems and linking INF-4873
Maya: thanks team. :thumbsup:
